name: APA 7 (professional paper)
description: The professional paper of the APA Publication Manual, 7th edition, for manuscripts sent to journals: a title page with author note, a running head of the shortened title in capitals, an abstract of at most 250 words; double spacing throughout and five levels of unnumbered headings.

source.name: APA Style, 7th ed.: Paper Format (apastyle.apa.org)
source.notes: Read from Internet Archive snapshots of the official APA Style pages, taken between 2026-03-30 (margins) and 2026-09-21 (the live site refuses automated requests); the date given is that of the snapshot of the main page. The page size is not stated: letter was chosen for a North American source. APA permits several fonts: sans serif 12 pt Aptos, 11 pt Calibri, 11 pt Arial, 10 pt Lucida Sans Unicode; serif 12 pt Times New Roman, 11 pt Georgia, 10 pt Computer Modern. Headings are in the type of the text; the source forbids extra blank lines above or below them, which is entered as 16.8pt, the distance between double-spaced lines of 12-point type. Footnotes are left by the source to the word processor's defaults ('usually single-spaced and a slightly smaller font'): 10 pt and single spacing are the general default. They may also be gathered on a page after the references. Not specified: file format, anonymisation. The running head is a shortened title of at most 50 characters, in capitals, flush left, without the label 'Running head:'; here the title itself is used, so a long title must be shortened by hand. The author note of the professional title page cannot be shown here. The label 'Keywords:' is italic and indented in the source. Of the fonts the source permits, Times New Roman is entered, being the one most manuscripts in the humanities are set in; any of the others may be chosen in its place.

limits.note: Abstract at most 250 words unless the journal says otherwise; three to five keywords. The source sets no limit on length and recommends counting words rather than pages.
